engine.meaning: Mostly the original, but the swaps garble technical terms: "An esky airmass will also have moved in" for a cooler airmass, "a stronger/deeper northern creek shortwave trough" for the northern stream, "RH paddocks show residual moisture" for RH fields. A forecaster's reader would be misled on those lines.
engine.sense: Several terms took the wrong sense: "An esky airmass" (cooler as a cool box), "northern creek" (stream as a watercourse), "RH paddocks" (fields as farmland), and "Highs will likely do it tough to get out of the 40s".
engine.authenticity: The few Aussie words are wrong-sense substitutions no Australian would say, and US forms remain: "An esky airmass", "a warm fall day".
engine.register: Largely untranslated for level 4: "A trailing cold front shifts across the region Wednesday with surface high pressure building in from the west through the day."
engine.tone: The dry technical tone survives where untouched ("Thursday will likely be dry, although cooler than Wednesday."), but the swaps make it accidentally comic: "RH paddocks show residual moisture within the cyclonic flow pattern."
engine.flow: Reads as the original, broken by nonsense phrases: "northern creek shortwave trough push across the Great Lakes".
engine.variety: Only a handful of substitutions, each a one-off: "esky", "creek", "do it tough", "paddocks".
engine.essence: Still recognisably the forecast discussion, "KEY MESSAGE 3...Low pressure system expected to bring rain Friday into early Saturday.", but marred by the garbled terms.

unharnessed.meaning: All the forecast points are kept, from "Might cop a stray shower Wednesday" to "The higher spots might drop into the upper 20s." One addition overstates: the lower levels are merely drier in the original, but here "drier than a dead dingo's donger". "the chances of heavy rain doing much damage are slim" is a fair reading of minimised impacts.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly fits ("Gusty nor'westers", "on the cards", "still a bit up in the air"), but "back up" for "support" strains each time: "which backs up drier conditions", "will back up deeper mixing", "enough to back up a few isolated showers".
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural ("moving along pretty smartly, so it won't be hanging about", "Expect a bloody cold night"), but one stock pub line is bolted onto a technical clause: "because the lower levels are drier than a dead dingo's donger".
unharnessed.register: A real retelling with swearing inside the dad dial ("a bloody cold night"), close to level 4 though the technical core is left as is: "The tighter gradient, and the CAA helping steepen lapse rates, will back up deeper mixing".
unharnessed.tone: The measured forecaster's voice mostly holds, but "drier than a dead dingo's donger" tips a technical point into a gag.
unharnessed.flow: Reads well: "A strong cold front barrels across the region by early Saturday morning, putting the northeast smack in a classic cold air advection pattern". "back up" repeats.
unharnessed.variety: Varied verbs and idiom ("slides", "shoving", "parking itself", "barrels", "on the cards"), with "back up" used three times.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the forecast discussion, key messages and model talk intact: "with the ECMWF and Canadian leaning wetter than the GFS solutions".

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every point is kept and the conversions are right: "tops in the 70s (21-26°C)", "0.25 and 0.60\" (6-15 mm)", "gusts 35-45 mph (55-70 km/h)", "the upper 20s (-2 to -3°C)". Asides react to the forecast: "Shorts weather, nearly.", "Dig the jumper out.", "Hang onto your hat.", "Rug up."
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "a westerly with a bit of go in it", "a few spits at most", "Best bet is it lobs in the Friday morning timeframe", "Saturday night'll be brass monkeys", "the whole box and dice".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian weather presenter ("don't go running for the brolly", "Exactly when the rain rocks up and when it clears off, that's still up in the air"), with a slightly staged opener: "Pull up a stool, here's the weather."
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-4 retelling with no swearing, within the dial: "Now here's where it gets interesting.", "it won't be hanging about all weekend like a bad smell".
yarn-troppo.tone: The forecaster's measured hedging is kept ("How much mixing and how strong that LLJ gets are still less certain this far out"), though the many asides push it chattier than the original's dry wit.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud well; the paragraph-closing tags ("Dig the jumper out.", "Rug up.") become a pattern.
yarn-troppo.variety: Widely varied: "a bit nippy", "brolly", "spits", "rocks up", "lobs in", "like a bad smell", "the whole box and dice", "brass monkeys", "Rug up".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the forecast discussion, "S word" joke kept: "it's a bit early to say the \"S word\" just yet (snow)."

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every point kept, conversions correct: "tops in the 70s (21-26°C)", "amounts closer to an inch (25 mm)", "the upper 20s (-2 to -3°C)".
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "a few spits at most", "when the rain rocks up", "Rain's more likely to lob in", "Tops will likely battle to get out of the 40s"; "backing drier weather" is a mild stretch.
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural where it changes things ("it won't be hanging about the whole weekend", "cos the lower levels are drier"), with nothing stock.
yarn-deadset.register: Light for level 4: much of the technical prose stands untouched, "The tighter gradient and CAA to help steepen lapse rates will back deeper mixing and so gusty NW winds."
yarn-deadset.tone: The measured forecaster tone comes through whole: "Expect a cold night Saturday night, with good odds of the interior dropping to at least freezing."
yarn-deadset.flow: Mostly smooth, one clunky join: "it'll be a light shower/a few spits at most".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the forecast discussion: "KEY MESSAGE 3...Low pressure system expected to bring rain Friday into early Saturday."

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point kept, conversions correct: "0.25 and 0.60\" (6-15 mm)", "gusts 35-45 mph (55-70 km/h)", "the upper 20s (-2 to -3°C)". "likely making it the coldest day of the season so far" is a fair rendering.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Every term fits: "925mb temperatures about 10C down on Wednesday", "a few spits at most", "the rain lobs in", "Tops'll likely battle to get out of the 40s".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian forecaster: "Put that westerly, downslope flow together with 925mb temperatures of +17- 18C and you get a warm autumn day", "Bit early to say the \"S word\" just yet (snow)."
yarn-dinkum.register: A real retelling, slightly lighter than level 4 in places: "The tighter gradient, and CAA to help steepen lapse rates, will back deeper mixing and so gusty NW winds."
yarn-dinkum.tone: The measured, hedged voice comes through whole: "are still a bit up in the air, since the guidance doesn't agree yet".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Most guidance has this system fairly progressive, so it won't be hanging about all weekend."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "a bit cool", "tops", "spits", "heaps of moisture, mind", "rocks up", "lobs in", "right across the board".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the forecast discussion, key messages and "S word" kept.

engine.quote: An esky airmass will also have moved in
engine.original: A cooler airmass will also have moved in
engine.why: "cooler" (comparative of cool) taken as a cool box; the line is nonsense.
The jet-stream branch rendered as a watercourse; wrong sense of a technical term.

engine.quote: Highs will likely do it tough to get out of the 40s
engine.original: Highs will likely struggle to get out of the 40s
engine.why: "do it tough" is about people enduring hardship; it does not take an infinitive and does not fit temperatures.
Left untranslated for a level-4 brief, US "fall" kept.

unharnessed.quote: because the lower levels are drier than a dead dingo's donger
unharnessed.original: due to the drier lower levels
unharnessed.why: A stock pub simile bolted on that exaggerates a comparative into bone dry and jars in a technical discussion.
"back up" for physical support strains and is repeated three times.

unharnessed.quote: highs in the 70s in plenty of spots
unharnessed.original: high temperatures in the 70s in many areas
unharnessed.why: Fahrenheit left unconverted; an Australian reader would not read 70s as warm without a Celsius figure.

yarn-troppo.quote: Pull up a stool, here's the weather.
yarn-troppo.why: A staged pub framing that renders nothing.
One of several closing tags ("Dig the jumper out.", "Hang onto your hat.") that turn into a formula.

yarn-deadset.quote: The tighter gradient and CAA to help steepen lapse rates will back deeper mixing and so gusty NW winds.
yarn-deadset.original: The tighter gradient and CAA to help steepen lapse rates will support deeper mixing and thus gusty NW winds.
yarn-deadset.why: Long technical stretches barely retold; noticeably lighter than level 4.

yarn-deadset.quote: a light shower/a few spits at most
yarn-deadset.why: The slash join reads awkwardly with the new idiom.

yarn-dinkum.quote: will back deeper mixing and so gusty NW winds
yarn-dinkum.original: will support deeper mixing and thus gusty NW winds
yarn-dinkum.why: Some technical stretches left close to the original; a little light for level 4.

summaries.engine: Barely translated, and its few swaps take the wrong sense and garble technical terms.
summaries.unharnessed: A good-weight retelling marred by one bolted-on stock simile and a repeated strained "back up".
summaries.yarn-troppo: The fullest and most varied retelling, accurate and helpfully converted, slightly over-tagged.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Accurate, natural and well converted, but on the light side of level 4.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Smooth, natural and accurate, with helpful conversions; a shade lighter than C.
